classification_rules.HIGH: Explicit exam directive: 'will be on the exam', 'memorize this', 'easy points', 'guaranteed', 'do not miss', 'key word for exam', 'torture you', 'if you remember nothing else', numerical fact called out as exam-required, triple repetition, boards love this
classification_rules.MEDIUM: Strong implicit signal: prof lingered, asked class, 'this is important', 'board pearl', class-participation drill, repeated twice
classification_rules.LOW: General pedagogical emphasis: framed as clinical competence, background context, awareness-level

items.topic: Case framework — 5-step DDx format
items.prof_intent: Prof walked class through the 5-step case format she uses for every patient scenario and repeated it at the start of each case — signaling it as the expected exam format
items.rendered_text_snippet: Describe the lesion, gather additional info, build a DDx (3-4), decide on tests, form a plan. Repeated at every case.

items.topic: Impetigo — honey-colored crusts descriptor
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged 'honey-colored crusts' and 'cornflakes glued to the surface' as slide yellow highlights translating directly to board exam targets. Both phrasings were used in the same breath.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Honey-colored crusts ('cornflakes glued on') — top visual exam item for impetigo.

items.topic: Impetigo — organism and age group
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized Staph aureus + streptococci as causative organisms and flagged '2-5 year olds' as testable
items.rendered_text_snippet: Staph aureus / beta-hemolytic strep; most common bacterial skin infection in 2-5 year olds.

items.topic: Impetigo — Augmentin dosing by weight
items.prof_intent: Prof singled out Augmentin as the drug dentists need to know from the impetigo treatment list
items.rendered_text_snippet: Augmentin (amoxicillin-clavulanic acid) — dose by WEIGHT not age; <40 kg = 25 mg/kg/d BID; ≥40 kg = 500 mg.

items.topic: Syphilis — 'chancre' vocabulary guaranteed on exam
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged 'chancre' (SHANK-er) as exam-guaranteed vocabulary and drilled the pronunciation explicitly. Tier-1 emphasis in source HTML.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Chancre = painless, indurated, clean-base ulcer of 1° syphilis. Pronunciation: SHANK-er. Will be on exam.

items.topic: Syphilis — 6-week false-negative serology window
items.prof_intent: Prof repeated this on two separate slides — double repetition signals guaranteed exam point
items.rendered_text_snippet: Syphilis serology may be NEGATIVE in the first 6 weeks after infection — false-negative window. Antibodies not yet detectable.

items.topic: Syphilis — incisional biopsy technique for suspected SCC
items.prof_intent: Prof asked the class what biopsy technique to use when SCC is on the differential — driving toward incisional biopsy of ulcer base AND edge
items.rendered_text_snippet: Incisional biopsy including both the ulcer base and the edge — correct approach for any suspicious non-healing oral ulcer.

items.topic: Syphilis 2° — split papules + condyloma lata as mandatory buzzwords
items.prof_intent: Prof called out split papules at oral commissures as classic quiz target and named condyloma lata as mandatory buzzword
items.rendered_text_snippet: 2° syphilis: split papules at commissures; condyloma lata (looks like papillomas). Both terms are board-exam mandatory.

items.topic: Syphilis 2° — mucous patches visual description
items.prof_intent: Prof described white elevated patches with gooey component as exam cue for 2° syphilis; paired with condyloma lata as mandatory buzzwords
items.rendered_text_snippet: Mucous patches = white, elevated, gooey component — visual exam cue for 2° syphilis. Condyloma lata co-present.

items.topic: Syphilis 3° — tabes dorsalis + gumma as board terms
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged tabes dorsalis as 'sexy' board term and gumma as mandatory. Tied palatal perforation directly to tertiary syphilis.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Tabes dorsalis (posterior spinal cord degeneration) = CNS sequela of tertiary syphilis. Gumma = granulomatous ball of inflammation. Palatal perforation → put tertiary syphilis on DDx.

items.topic: Mandatory reportable diseases — will be on exam
items.prof_intent: Prof stated directly that mandatory reportable diseases will be on the exam. Triple 'please' urgency language used. Students were asked to practice the list.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Mandatory reportable diseases — DPH notification required. Syphilis + TB both reportable. This WILL be on the exam.

items.topic: Syphilis treatment — intramuscular penicillin G
items.prof_intent: Prof drilled IM penicillin G across two separate case discussions — drug-disease pairing is guaranteed exam association
items.rendered_text_snippet: Syphilis treatment: Benzathine Penicillin G 2.4 MU IM x1. Drug-disease pairing is a guaranteed exam association.

items.topic: TB — isoniazid + rifampin appear on every exam
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged isoniazid and rifampin as highest exam priority in entire lecture — 'appear on every exam.' Both present in BOTH phases = 6-month total.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Isoniazid + rifampin — present in both phases (PIRE x8 wk + IR x16 wk). 6-month total course. Appears on every exam.

items.topic: TB — DOT (Directly Observed Therapy)
items.prof_intent: Prof explained DOT as public health protocol where nurse watches every pill. Know acronym and clinical meaning.
items.rendered_text_snippet: DOT = Directly Observed Therapy. Nurse witnesses every dose to ensure compliance. TB only.

items.topic: TB — miliary TB and calcified cervical lymph nodes on panoramic
items.prof_intent: Prof explained miliary TB etymology and connected calcified cervical nodes to panoramic radiographic finding
items.rendered_text_snippet: Miliary TB — calcified foci look like millet seeds; can appear as calcified cervical lymph nodes on panoramic X-ray.

items.topic: TB — DPH reportable, triple 'please' emphasis
items.prof_intent: Triple 'please' urgency — highest urgency signal used in the lecture. TB joins syphilis as DPH-reportable.
items.rendered_text_snippet: TB is mandatorily reportable to MA DPH — same highest-urgency signal as syphilis. Both on DPH list.

items.topic: TB — clinical action sequence in dental setting
items.prof_intent: Prof classified TB as medical urgency and gave clinical action sequence: isolate → notify DPH → refer to ID
items.rendered_text_snippet: TB: immediate isolation, do not treat in open dental bays. Aerosol + isolation protocols. Isolate → notify DPH → refer to ID.

items.topic: Candidiasis — DDx for white plaques that wipe off
items.prof_intent: Prof walked through DDx for white plaques that wipe off — standard exam format question
items.rendered_text_snippet: White plaques that wipe off DDx: pseudomembranous candidiasis (top), then strep throat, herpangina, gonorrhea.

items.topic: Xerostomia vs hyposalivation — must know distinction
items.prof_intent: Prof stated students MUST know this distinction. Exam-tested in multiple lectures. Tier-1 flag.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Xerostomia = subjective (sensation). Hyposalivation = objective (measurable). Only hyposalivation causes dental complications. NOT synonyms.

items.topic: Candidiasis types table — all types will be tested
items.prof_intent: Prof placed blanket responsibility on class for knowing all candidiasis clinical types. 'You will be tested on all of this.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: All 6 candidiasis subtypes are testable: pseudomembranous, erythematous, median rhomboid, angular cheilitis, denture stomatitis, hyperplastic (cannot wipe off → biopsy).

items.topic: Median rhomboid glossitis — kissing lesion on palate
items.prof_intent: Prof double-emphasized ('almost almost always') that central papillary atrophy self-inoculates palate — guaranteed exam clinical pearl
items.rendered_text_snippet: Central papillary atrophy (median rhomboid glossitis) → ALWAYS check the palate. Kissing lesion on opposing palate. Guaranteed exam pearl.

items.topic: Antifungal medications — asked on exams every single year
items.prof_intent: Prof stated antifungal medications are asked every single year — tier-1 mandatory memorization
items.rendered_text_snippet: Clotrimazole, nystatin, miconazole, fluconazole — the four mandatory antifungal names. Asked on exams every year.

items.topic: Clotrimazole contraindicated in diabetics — will be on exam
items.prof_intent: Prof stated this THREE times in a row and explicitly said she would ask it on an exam. Single most emphatic repetition in candidiasis section.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Clotrimazole (Mycelex) troches = HIGH SUGAR → contraindicated in diabetic patients. Use nystatin instead. WILL be on exam.

items.topic: Azole antifungals — hepatotoxicity via CYP450 (azole → liver)
items.prof_intent: Prof triple-drilled the azole-liver association as a rhythm to memorize. Tier-2 flag but triple repetition.
items.rendered_text_snippet: All -azoles → check LFTs. Hepatotoxicity via CYP450 interactions. Rhythm: azole → liver.

items.topic: Angular cheilitis — Mycolog II 'bread and butter dentistry'
items.prof_intent: Prof called angular cheilitis 'bread and butter dentistry' — boards expect it. Treatment is Mycolog II (nystatin + triamcinolone acetonide).
items.rendered_text_snippet: Angular cheilitis: Mycolog II BID (nystatin + triamcinolone acetonide). Covers both fungal + inflammatory components. Boards expect this.

items.topic: HHV 1-8 taxonomy — fair game on exam
items.prof_intent: Prof signaled HHV 1-8 taxonomy as fair game with her own mnemonic system for anchoring each virus
items.rendered_text_snippet: HHV1=above belt; HHV2=below belt; HHV3=VZV (Z=3 strokes); HHV4=EBV (Barr=4 letters); HHV5=CMV (cinco). All testable.

items.topic: VZV — V1 vs V2 distribution with ocular risk
items.prof_intent: Prof required students to know V1 vs V2 herpes zoster distinction — V1 involvement carries ocular risk. Tier-1 flag.
items.rendered_text_snippet: V1 zoster → ophthalmic branch → ocular risk → always ask about vision. V2 = maxillary. Distinction is clinically critical.

items.topic: Hutchinson's sign vs optic keratitis distinction
items.prof_intent: Prof distinguished Hutchinson's sign (VZV, nasal tip, potentially blinding) from optic keratitis (HSV, less severe)
items.rendered_text_snippet: Hutchinson sign = nasal tip VZV → nasociliary branch → HZO → corneal ulceration → blindness. Mandatory ophtho referral.

items.topic: HSV — pinhead vesicles on erythematous base as defining morphology
items.prof_intent: Prof stated 'important' twice and highlighted it twice on the slide for this descriptor
items.rendered_text_snippet: Primary HSV morphology: pinhead vesicles coalescing on erythematous base → ulcers on keratinized mucosa.

items.topic: HSV transmissibility peaks at vesicle rupture — stop dentistry
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized vesicle rupture as exact moment dentistry must stop. Both clinical safety and exam-tested infection control.
items.rendered_text_snippet: HSV transmissibility HIGHEST when vesicles rupture. Do NOT perform dental procedures on patient with active ruptured HSV vesicles.

items.topic: HSV prodrome — 6-24 hour window before vesicles
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged prodrome as clinically important for determining whether 48-hour antiviral window is still open
items.rendered_text_snippet: HSV prodrome: 6-24 hours of itching/tingling/warmth/erythema before vesicle formation. Window for antiviral starts here.

items.topic: HSV — 48-hour antiviral treatment window
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized 48-hour window as key clinical decision point and said she will test it in case format
items.rendered_text_snippet: Must start acyclovir/valacyclovir within 48 hours of prodrome onset. This is a case-format clinical reasoning question.

items.topic: HSV in children — lidocaine (seizures) and benzocaine (methemoglobinemia) contraindicated
items.prof_intent: Prof called these two pediatric contraindications high-yield exam traps when HSV question involves a child
items.rendered_text_snippet: AVOID in pediatrics: topical lidocaine (seizures) AND topical benzocaine (methemoglobinemia). High-yield exam trap for HSV child cases.

items.topic: CMV — necrotic ulcer in immunocompromised
items.prof_intent: Prof formally introduced 'necrotic' and used the term 5 times. CMV = deep ulcer with abundant dead tissue debris.
items.rendered_text_snippet: CMV oral ulcer descriptor = necrotic (deep + heavily debridated + dead tissue). Immunocompromised patients.

items.topic: CMV — GI pain in immunocompromised distinguishes from TB
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged GI pain as distinguishing feature for CMV vs TB in immunocompromised differential
items.rendered_text_snippet: CMV is viscerotropic → GI pain in immunocompromised patient favors CMV over TB or deep fungal.

items.topic: CMV treatment — valganciclovir 900 mg; dentist role is referral only
items.prof_intent: Prof made clear valganciclovir is the treatment but dentist's role is referral to ID, not prescribing. Tier-1 flag.
items.rendered_text_snippet: CMV: valganciclovir 900 mg PO BID (acyclovir FAILS). Dentist's role = refer to Infectious Disease. Do NOT prescribe antiviral yourself.

items.topic: Exam format guaranteed — photo + DDx + workup + treatment plan
items.prof_intent: Prof stated she will include a typed clinical question with photo + DDx + workup format. Tier-1 explicit guarantee.
items.rendered_text_snippet: EXAM FORMAT GUARANTEED: photo + describe lesion + DDx + workup + treatment plan. Practice this framework for every L2 disease.

items.topic: RAS — erythematous halo is easy exam point
items.prof_intent: Prof stated recognition of erythematous halo gets immediate credit — 'easy exam point'
items.rendered_text_snippet: RAS: erythematous halo around ulcer = easy exam point. Recognize this in a photo for immediate credit.

items.topic: RAS — location (keratinized vs non-keratinized) distinguishes from HSV
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized location as most critical differentiator — keratinized mucosa = HSV, non-keratinized = RAS
items.rendered_text_snippet: RAS: NON-keratinized mucosa ONLY. HSV: keratinized mucosa. Location is the key differentiator on exam.

items.topic: RAS — new onset after age 40 requires workup
items.prof_intent: Prof stressed new-onset ulcers after 40 in a patient with no childhood history is not normal
items.rendered_text_snippet: New-onset RAS-like ulcers after age 40 with no childhood history = workup required. Not normal.

items.topic: RAS — 'herpetiform' is morphologic term only, NOT caused by HSV
items.prof_intent: Prof called this a red herring on exams explicitly. Tier-1 exam trap.
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: Herpetiform aphthae = morphologic descriptor only. NOT caused by Herpes Simplex Virus. Immune-mediated.

items.topic: Dexamethasone solution — 'torture' students, most important prescription
items.prof_intent: Prof stated she would 'torture' students about dexamethasone solution — single most important prescription for every dentist
items.rendered_text_snippet: Dexamethasone elixir 0.5 mg/5 mL swish and spit BID — prof's most important oral medicine prescription. Will torture students about this.

items.topic: Triamcinolone acetonide — WEAKEST steroid trap
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap explicitly labeled. Triamcinolone has 'dental' in name but is the weakest of the three common oral medicine corticosteroids.
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: Triamcinolone acetonide dental paste = WEAKEST corticosteroid for oral medicine despite 'dental' in name. Do not default to it.

items.topic: Sensodyne is NOT SLS-free — do not recommend for mucosal conditions
items.prof_intent: Prof directly warned against recommending Sensodyne for mucosal conditions; named Doctor Bob as top SLS-free recommendation
items.rendered_text_snippet: Sensodyne is NOT SLS-free. Do not recommend for aphthous/mucosal conditions. Use Doctor Bob (SLS-free) instead.

items.topic: Geographic tongue — 3 Ds: Depapillated, Demarcated, Dynamic
items.prof_intent: Prof had entire class verbally repeat each of the three D's — class participation drill for exam mnemonic
items.rendered_text_snippet: Geographic tongue: 3 D's = Depapillated, Demarcated, Dynamic (migratory). Class said these out loud together.

items.topic: Geographic tongue — 'serpiginous' is key vocabulary for exam
items.prof_intent: Prof had entire class say 'serpiginous' out loud in lecture, calling it key vocabulary for the exam
items.rendered_text_snippet: Serpiginous = snake-like wavy border of geographic tongue. Key vocabulary word — class said it aloud.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: Serpiginous border on geographic tongue = does NOT wipe off and does NOT respond to antifungals — exam trap vs. candidiasis

items.topic: Geographic tongue vs candidiasis trap — white border does not scrape off
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap: serpiginous white border of GT does NOT scrape off with gauze and does NOT respond to antifungals
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP 1: Geographic tongue white border ≠ candidiasis. Candida scrapes off. GT border does NOT. TRAP 2: GT can appear on buccal mucosa (ectopic = erythema migrans).

items.topic: Erythroplakia — very high likelihood of malignancy at first diagnosis
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged erythroplakia as having very high malignancy likelihood on first diagnosis and 'must not be missed'
items.rendered_text_snippet: Erythroplakia: very high likelihood of malignancy at first diagnosis. ~75-90% already severe dysplasia/CIS/SCC at first biopsy. Do not miss.

items.topic: Drug gingival hyperplasia — boards love asking about it; memorize the drugs
items.prof_intent: Prof explicitly told students boards love asking about DRGH and the specific drugs — recommended complete memorization
items.rendered_text_snippet: DRGH: Phenytoin ~50%, cyclosporine 25-70%, nifedipine/amlodipine 6-25%. Onset 1-3 months. Starts at interdental papillae. Boards love this.

items.topic: DRGH — onset 1-3 months and starts at interdental papillae
items.prof_intent: Prof gave onset timeline as direct exam target — 1-3 months and starting at interdental papillae
items.rendered_text_snippet: DRGH onset: 1-3 months after starting drug. Starts at interdental papillae first.

items.topic: DRGH — do NOT go straight to gingivectomy without correcting drug and hygiene
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap: surgery without correcting causative drug and optimizing hygiene means tissue grows right back
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: Never go straight to gingivectomy for DRGH. Drug change + plaque control FIRST — otherwise tissue grows back.

items.topic: Patch test — positive means sensitization history, not necessarily active trigger
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap: positive patch test requires temporal correlation, not sole causation
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: Positive patch test = sensitization history only. Requires temporal correlation with symptoms to confirm active trigger.

items.topic: TLP — reassurance is primary management
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized reassurance as primary management approach for TLP — first-line exam answer
items.rendered_text_snippet: TLP (transient lingual papillitis): self-limited 2-15 days. First-line management = reassurance.

items.topic: OLP — auto-inflammatory NOT autoimmune (prof's exam distinction)
items.prof_intent: Prof stated this distinction beyond the slide: 'auto-inflammatory' is correct on HER exam, not 'autoimmune'
items.rendered_text_snippet: OLP = auto-inflammatory (T-cell mediated), NOT autoimmune. Prof explicitly corrects this distinction on her exam.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: OLP classification on this exam: auto-inflammatory (not autoimmune). The T-cell-mediated mechanism is idiopathic, not antibody-driven.

items.topic: OLP — bilateral pathognomonic; unilateral = biopsy
items.prof_intent: Prof noted bilateral location is key exam feature; unilateral = biopsy to exclude dysplasia
items.rendered_text_snippet: OLP: bilateral posterior buccal mucosa = classic + reassuring. Unilateral OR atypical location = biopsy to exclude dysplasia.

items.topic: OLP — 4 P's mnemonic for cutaneous LP
items.prof_intent: Prof described 4 P's as memory tool and said she checks wrists/ankles in her own practice
items.rendered_text_snippet: Cutaneous LP = 4 P's: Purple, Polygonal, Pruritic Papules. Check wrists and ankles to support OLP diagnosis.

items.topic: OLP — clobetasol + dexamethasone for erosive OLP: easy guaranteed exam question
items.prof_intent: Prof called this an 'easy guaranteed exam question' — both drugs must be known for erosive OLP
items.rendered_text_snippet: Erosive OLP treatment: clobetasol 0.05% gel + dexamethasone elixir swish and spit BID. 'Easy guaranteed exam question.'

items.topic: OLP — steroids on vermilion lip cause fat pad loss; use tacrolimus
items.prof_intent: Prof gave this as a hard clinical rule — applying steroids to vermilion lip causes permanent cosmetic deformity
items.rendered_text_snippet: HARD RULE: Never apply corticosteroids to vermilion lip. Permanent fat pad loss/cosmetic deformity. Use tacrolimus for lip OLP.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: Lip OLP: use tacrolimus, NOT topical steroids. Steroids on vermilion = irreversible fat pad atrophy.

items.topic: MMP — ophtho referral is a 'do not miss'; ALL patients even asymptomatic
items.prof_intent: Prof described ophtho referral rule as 'do not miss' — 60-70% have ocular involvement and scarring is irreversible
items.rendered_text_snippet: MMP: REFER ALL PATIENTS to ophthalmology even if asymptomatic. 61-70% ocular involvement. Symblepharon/blindness risk.

items.topic: MMP — anti-laminin 332 triggers malignancy workup
items.prof_intent: Prof said 'already have it' twice — anti-laminin 332 = 25% risk of adenocarcinoma → immediate malignancy workup
items.rendered_text_snippet: Anti-laminin 332 antibodies in MMP = 25% associated with adenocarcinoma. Triggers immediate malignancy workup.

items.topic: IgA/IgG/C3 in immunobullous diseases — location is the testable fact
items.prof_intent: Prof said boards love to ask about IgA/IgG/C3 in immunobullous diseases — linear at BMZ = MMP, intercellular = PV
items.rendered_text_snippet: MMP: linear IgG/IgA/C3 at BMZ (deep). PV: chicken-wire intercellular IgG (intraepithelial). Location = the testable fact.

items.topic: PV — 'oral lesions are first to show, last to go'
items.prof_intent: Prof said this phrase with strong professional pride emphasis — dentist's position to catch disease early
items.rendered_text_snippet: PV: 'Oral lesions are first to show, last to go.' Dentist can diagnose PV before dermatologist. >50% oral-first.

items.topic: PV — DSG3 vs DSG1 trap
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap: DSG3 = oral only; DSG1 = skin only; both DSG3+DSG1 = oral AND skin involvement
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: DSG3 = oral lesions only; DSG1 = skin lesions only; DSG3 + DSG1 = both oral AND skin. Don't blur these.

items.topic: PV — biopsying early saves lives
items.prof_intent: Prof stated early biopsy before treatment = how lives get saved
items.rendered_text_snippet: PV: biopsy early and BEFORE treatment. Perilesional tissue + Michel solution. Faster diagnosis = easier treatment.

items.topic: EM vs SJS — NOT a spectrum (prof's explicit exam position)
items.prof_intent: Prof called the spectrum concept 'old, old thought process' and told students to abandon it — separate entities on HER exam
items.rendered_text_snippet: EM and SJS are SEPARATE diseases on this exam, NOT a spectrum. Different etiologies. Prof will mark spectrum-concept answers wrong.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: EM = infection-triggered (HSV ~70%); SJS = drug-triggered (~85%). Not a spectrum — separate diseases with different management and prognosis.

items.topic: EM/SJS — infection vs drug trigger determines everything
items.prof_intent: Prof called this the central clinical logic of the entire EM/SJS section — infection vs drug = prognosis and urgency
items.rendered_text_snippet: EM: HSV-triggered ~70%, self-limited. SJS: drug-triggered ~85%, potentially life-threatening. Trigger = the fork in the road.

items.topic: SJS — topical lidocaine in children absorbed through inflamed mucosa = seizures
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged this as specific exam trap for pediatric SJS case questions
items.rendered_text_snippet: Pediatric SJS: topical lidocaine absorbed through inflamed mucosa → toxic serum levels → seizures. Use benzocaine instead.

items.topic: SJS/TEN — allopurinol has highest absolute risk; carbamazepine requires HLA screening in Han Chinese
items.prof_intent: Prof said if students remember only one drug it should be allopurinol. Also flagged carbamazepine for TN treatment → HLA-B*15:01 screening required
items.rendered_text_snippet: SJS/TEN highest-risk drug = allopurinol. Carbamazepine (used for trigeminal neuralgia): HLA-B*15:01 screening required in Han Chinese patients.

items.topic: SCORTEN predicts survival — 5+ points = likely death
items.prof_intent: Prof described SCORTEN as survival predictor
items.rendered_text_snippet: SCORTEN score: 5+ points = likely death; 1-3 = likely survival. Used for TEN prognosis.

items.topic: SJS — dentist's role: recognition and stopping the drug
items.prof_intent: Prof described dentist's role as recognition and stopping the drug — 4-step approach
items.rendered_text_snippet: SJS: Dentist's role = recognize + stop all suspected drugs immediately. Refer to ED. Every hour matters.

items.topic: PAMS — boards-tested even though rarely seen
items.prof_intent: Prof said this is boards-tested even though students will rarely see these patients in practice
items.rendered_text_snippet: PAMS: always associated with malignancy (NHL ~40%, CLL ~20%, Castleman ~18%). Bronchiolitis obliterans = #1 cause of death. Mortality 60-90%.

items.topic: Plasma cell gingivitis — verbatim phrasing expected on exam
items.prof_intent: Prof stated the phrase 'Generalized erythema and edema of the maxillary and mandibular facial gingiva' is expected verbatim on exam
items.rendered_text_snippet: EXPECTED ON EXAM: 'Generalized erythema and edema of the maxillary and mandibular facial gingiva.' Say maxilla/mandible, not jaw. Cause = cinnamon/benzoate contact reaction.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: Plasma cell gingivitis verbatim descriptor: 'Generalized erythema and edema of the maxillary and mandibular FACIAL gingiva.' Fire-engine red, NO Wickham striae. Trigger: cinnamaldehyde + benzoate avoidance = treatment.

items.topic: Plasma cell gingivitis — IBS ≠ IBD distinction
items.prof_intent: Prof explicitly stated 'IBS is not IBD' as a distractor trap in the PCG case
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: IBS (irritable bowel) = no oral manifestations. IBD (Crohn's/UC) = oral facial granulomatosis. Don't let patient's IBS history mislead you.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: IBS ≠ IBD trap: IBS = functional GI disorder, ZERO oral manifestations. IBD (Crohn's) = inflammatory, oral facial granulomatosis possible.

items.topic: Heck disease — HPV 13/32 not covered by Gardasil 9 ('they love asking this on the boards')
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'They love asking this on the boards. You have to know 1332. They love that current vaccines do not protect against 13 and 32.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: Heck disease = HPV 13/32. NOT covered by Gardasil 9. Can get Heck disease even if fully vaccinated. Boards love this.

items.topic: Carcinoma in situ is NOT a pre-cancer — it IS cancer
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'Some people think CIS is a pre-cancer. It's not, it's cancer. It's just the second before it invades.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: CIS = full-thickness epithelial atypia, basement membrane intact. It IS cancer, NOT pre-cancer. Next step = invasion = SCC.

items.topic: Oral epidemiology numbers — 36,600 new / 12,230 deaths / >50% with mets at diagnosis
items.prof_intent: Prof's anchor numbers — prof opened with these and returned to them. Memorize block in source HTML.
items.rendered_text_snippet: 36,600 new oral cavity cancers/yr; 12,230 deaths/yr; >50% present with metastatic disease at diagnosis. Oral tongue 41.7% #1 site.

items.topic: Inherited syndromes — 'they love to ask this on the board'
items.prof_intent: Board pearl verbatim: 'Inherited syndromes — they love to ask this on the board.' List: Fanconi anemia, dyskeratosis congenita, Li-Fraumeni, Cowden, xeroderma pigmentosum.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Fanconi anemia (OR ~40.6), dyskeratosis congenita, Li-Fraumeni, Cowden, xeroderma pigmentosum. Know all 5 names — boards love inherited syndromes.

items.topic: Tobacco + alcohol = ~30x (multiplicative NOT additive)
items.prof_intent: Prof's key teaching point — ~30x combined risk is multiplicative, not additive (5x × 6x, not 5x + 6x)
items.rendered_text_snippet: Tobacco + alcohol = ~30x risk, MULTIPLICATIVE not additive. Alcohol dehydrates mucosa → carcinogens penetrate deeper.

items.topic: Leukoplakia requires biopsy — clinical sensitivity 60%, specificity 62%
items.prof_intent: Prof stated leukoplakia always requires biopsy; clinical judgment alone cannot reliably detect cancer by eye
items.rendered_text_snippet: Leukoplakia: always biopsy. Clinical sensitivity 60%, specificity 62% — you cannot reliably tell malignant from benign by eye.

items.topic: 39.6% of progressors had NO dysplasia on first biopsy — never 'done'
items.prof_intent: Prof emphasized this paradox in a separate callout: 'Read that twice.' Never discharge after one benign biopsy.
items.rendered_text_snippet: 39.6% of leukoplakias that progressed to SCC had only 'hyperkeratosis without dysplasia' on original biopsy. NEVER dismiss after one benign read.

items.topic: Erythroplakia — ~75-90% already severe dysplasia/CIS/SCC at first biopsy; median time to cancer 3.7 months
items.prof_intent: Two separate statistics: 50% MT rate overall + 75-90% already advanced at first biopsy. Median time 3.7 months = urgent referral. Board pearl verbatim: 'Biopsy, biopsy, biopsy.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: Erythroplakia: ~50% MT rate. ~75-90% already severe dysplasia/CIS/SCC at first biopsy. Median time to cancer: 3.7 months vs leukoplakia 25 months. Urgent referral.

items.topic: PVL — 'ring around the collar' + 48-50% MT + 8x higher than conventional
items.prof_intent: Prof used 'ring around the collar' as clinical mnemonic for circumferential gingival PVL. 8x higher MT rate than conventional leukoplakia.
items.rendered_text_snippet: PVL: gingiva most common ('ring around the collar'). MT rate 48-50%, up to 100% lifetime. Annual rate 9.3%. 8x higher than conventional leukoplakia. F:M 2:1, non-smokers.

items.topic: Biopsy site selection mnemonic — 'Red over white, edge over center, deep for verrucous, multiple for big'
items.prof_intent: Prof's own mnemonic explicitly stated in source. Listed in notecard v2 master strip.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Biopsy mnemonic: 'Red over white, edge over center, deep for verrucous, multiple for big.' Tumor seeding = myth (FNA ~0.00012%).

items.topic: DOI ≥5 mm = T2 staging; biopsy must reach 4-6 mm
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'If you have a depth of invasion that's 5 millimeters, then you're already in T2. You better be at around 4 or 5 millimeters.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: DOI ≥5 mm = T2. Biopsy must reach 4-6 mm deep. Superficial punch misses invasive front and gives artificially low DOI reading.

items.topic: DOI >4 mm = automatic neck dissection
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'If it's more than 4 millimeters, the patient automatically gets a neck dissection. So you need to go deep.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: DOI >4 mm = elective neck dissection. Biopsy depth has DIRECT surgical staging consequences. Punch to 4-6 mm.

items.topic: No brush biopsies — cannot assess architecture
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'This is why brush biopsies don't work...No brush biopsies.' Cannot assess architectural/organizational changes that define dysplasia.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Brush biopsy (OralCDx) = cytology only. CANNOT assess architectural changes defining dysplasia. Negative brush biopsy does NOT rule out dysplasia. NO brush biopsies.

items.topic: Chemoprevention tables — 'You don't have to know anything from these tables'
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'You don't have to know anything from these tables.' Explicitly dismissed detailed chemoprevention data for exam.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Chemoprevention detailed tables = NOT exam-tested. Know: imiquimod = TLR-7 agonist. ALA-PDT = 66-100% CR. Goal = cancer prevention, not plaque elimination.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: Chemoprevention: tables not tested. Testable concepts only: (1) imiquimod = TLR-7 agonist; (2) ALA-PDT = 66-100% CR; (3) beta-carotene may increase risk in smokers (CARET trial).

items.topic: 'You don't have to get rid of the leukoplakia to have a win'
items.prof_intent: Verbatim from Case 2 caption. Treatment goal = cancer prevention, not plaque elimination.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Treatment goal for dysplasia: 'You don't have to get rid of the leukoplakia to have a win.' Goal = stable, cancer-free. Imiquimod sustained response at 3+ years.

items.topic: OLP as OPMD — prof's contested position ('toe to toe')
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'I will stand toe to toe with people about this. I don't think it's a potentially malignant condition.' Know BOTH positions for exam.
items.rendered_text_snippet: WHO: OLP IS an OPMD (~1.4% MT). Prof's position: OLP transformation cases were misdiagnosed oral lichenoid dysplasia. Know BOTH on exam. Safe: rank OLP at BOTTOM of OPMD list.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: OLP-OPMD controversy: WHO lists OLP as OPMD at 1.4% MT. Prof disagrees — she believes these cases were oral lichenoid dysplasia all along. On exam: OLP IS on OPMD lists; rank it lowest (0.2-1.4%).

items.topic: Tumor thickness vs depth of invasion — NOT the same thing for T-staging
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap explicitly labeled: exophytic component above mucosa does NOT count toward DOI
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: Tumor thickness ≠ DOI. DOI = measured from adjacent NORMAL mucosal baseline DOWNWARD. Exophytic 'warty stuff on top' does NOT count. Exam note: don't memorize N2a/N2b/N2c subcategories.

items.topic: Stage I SCC = 80-90% 5-yr OS; Stage IVC (<20%) — one-way ticket
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'Stage one has excellent 5-year survival 80-90%, but as soon as anything metastasizes out, that's stage 4C, less than 20% survival.'
items.rendered_text_snippet: Stage I oral SCC = ~85% 5-yr OS. Stage IVC (any M1) = <20% 5-yr OS. 'One-way ticket to Stage 4C.'

items.topic: HPV+ survival benefit is OROPHARYNX-specific, NOT oral cavity
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'Unfortunately in the oral cavity having HPV doesn't give you a better prognosis.' Two consecutive exam traps labeled tier-1.
items.rendered_text_snippet: HPV+ OPSCC (tonsil/BOT): ~80-85% 5-yr OS. HPV+ OCSCC (oral cavity): NO survival benefit. p16 IHC = reliable surrogate in OROPHARYNX only.

items.topic: Gardasil 9 — 'get them tattooed on your butt; you gotta know these 9'
items.prof_intent: Verbatim: 'Get them tattooed on your butt. You gotta know these 9.' CONFIRMED quiz question per board pearl.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Gardasil 9 covers: 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, 58. NOT covered: HPV 13/32 (Heck) and HPV 2/4 (verruca). CONFIRMED quiz question.

items.topic: Horseshoe of Death — lateral tongue + FOM + soft palate = examine every visit
items.prof_intent: Prof said 'If you're not flipping that tongue around...you are not practicing standard of care.' Stated tongue is #1 site 3 times during lecture.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Horseshoe of Death: lateral/ventral tongue (42%) + FOM (16%) + soft palate. Examine EVERY visit. Standard of care.

items.topic: ~50% of oral SCCs are non-ulcerated at diagnosis; induration = most reliable sign
items.prof_intent: Tier-1 exam trap: don't anchor on 'oral cancer = ulcer.' Induration on palpation is most reliable physical finding.
items.rendered_text_snippet: TRAP: ~50% of oral SCC at diagnosis are NON-ulcerated. Induration on palpation = most reliable physical finding. Do not anchor on ulcer.

items.topic: AJCC 8th edition — DOI added to T-staging + ENE added to N-staging
items.prof_intent: Prof called out both big changes in 8th edition as exam-required knowledge. N3b = ENE+ = worst nodal stage.
items.rendered_text_snippet: AJCC 8th ed changes: (1) DOI added to T-stage. (2) ENE added to N-stage (N3b = ENE+ = worst; gets adjuvant CRT).

items.topic: Field cancerization — incisional biopsy can underestimate grade
items.prof_intent: High-yield callout: incisional biopsy showed moderate dysplasia but excision revealed focal severe dysplasia
items.rendered_text_snippet: Incisional biopsies can UNDERESTIMATE true grade. Excision may reveal higher-grade dysplasia. Field cancerization = recurrence at prior excision margin.

items.topic: Verrucous carcinoma — superficial biopsy cannot diagnose it
items.prof_intent: Exam trap: must biopsy to deep submucosa to see pushing border. Diagnosis depends on architecture not cytology.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Verrucous carcinoma: superficial biopsy misses the diagnosis. Must include deep submucosa to see the PUSHING border. No distant mets in pure form.

items.topic: Sjögren ACR-EULAR ≥4 points — threshold is guaranteed exam target
items.prof_intent: Prof explicitly called out ≥4 point threshold as guaranteed exam target. Biopsy = 3 pts; anti-SSA = 3 pts.
items.rendered_text_snippet: ACR-EULAR 2016 Sjögren criteria: ≥4 points for classification. Biopsy (focal lymphocytic sialadenitis) = 3 pts. Anti-SSA(Ro) = 3 pts. Anti-SSB = 1 pt.

items.topic: Sjögren MALT lymphoma risk — 5-10% lifetime; unilateral swelling = red flag; guaranteed boards question
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged Sjögren MALT lymphoma risk as 'guaranteed boards question' — memorize 5-10% lifetime risk and unilateral swelling as red flag
items.rendered_text_snippet: Sjögren: 5-10% lifetime risk of MALT lymphoma (NHL). 7-19x general population risk. Unilateral persistent salivary gland swelling = red flag for malignant transformation.

items.topic: Xerostomia vs hyposalivation — 'easy exam questions'
items.prof_intent: Prof called this distinction 'easy exam questions' — not subtle but guaranteed. Only hyposalivation causes dental damage.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Hyposalivation = objective. Xerostomia = subjective. ONLY hyposalivation causes caries, candidiasis, etc. Xerostomia alone does NOT cause caries.

items.topic: Radiation-induced caries pattern — high-frequency boards question
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged radiation caries pattern as 'high-frequency boards question' — all 6 features are slide-highlighted
items.rendered_text_snippet: Radiation caries: ipsilateral, cervical, smooth surfaces, mandibular anteriors + maxillary molars. Recall Q3-4 mo. PreviDent 5000 daily.

items.topic: M3 receptors — exams love asking about muscarinic subtypes
items.prof_intent: Prof singled out M3 as most important muscarinic subtype and flagged that exams love asking about nicotinic and muscarinic receptor subtypes
items.rendered_text_snippet: M3 receptor = target of sialagogues (secretion + smooth muscle). Pilocarpine = highest M3 affinity. CIs: asthma, glaucoma, cardiac.

items.topic: 10 functions of saliva — 'favorite board question; will test myself'
items.prof_intent: Prof called 10 functions of saliva a 'favorite board question' AND said she would test it herself. Memorize all 10 by first word.
items.rendered_text_snippet: 10 functions of saliva — favorite board question. Memorize all 10. Hub-and-spoke diagram is the single most testable saliva-function content.
items.suggested_better_paraphrase: 10 saliva functions: lubrication, digestion (amylase), antimicrobial, buffering/pH, remineralization, taste solvent, wound healing, speaking/swallowing, immune surveillance, dental pellicle formation. Board favorite + prof's own exam.

items.topic: Urological anticholinergics (oxybutynin OR 18.9) — highest drug class for hyposalivation
items.prof_intent: Prof flagged urological anticholinergics as highest-risk drug class (OR 18.9) and polypharmacy >3 meds (OR 2.9) as independent risk factor
items.rendered_text_snippet: Oxybutynin (anticholinergic) OR 18.9 = highest single drug class for hyposalivation. >3 medications = OR 2.9 independent of specific drug.

items.topic: Sialolithiasis — early stones not radiopaque; reason for ultrasound/CT
items.prof_intent: Prof explained pathophysiology: mucin plugs → mineral accumulation = reason early stones are not yet radiopaque on plain film
items.rendered_text_snippet: Sialolith pathophysiology: mucin plugs → mineral accumulation. Early stones NOT radiopaque → order ultrasound or CT when stone suspected but not seen on X-ray.

items.topic: Clotrimazole contraindicated in diabetics — cross-referenced with L1
items.prof_intent: Prof signaled this would reappear on future exams. Cross-references the L1 triple-drill. Same concept in both lectures.
items.rendered_text_snippet: Clotrimazole troches = HIGH SUGAR → contraindicated in diabetics. Cross-reference with L1 (triple-drilled). WILL reappear on exams.

items.topic: Vaseline/Aquaphor AVOID for dry mouth — use Lanolin HPA
items.prof_intent: Prof made Vaseline/Aquaphor avoidance 'a personal clinical hill' — guaranteed clinical-recommendation exam question
items.rendered_text_snippet: AVOID Vaseline and Aquaphor for dry mouth/lips: fully occlusive, worsen candidiasis, flammable. Use Lanolin HPA (Lansinoh) instead.

items.topic: Hyposalivation sequelae — 'easy exam questions'
items.prof_intent: Prof called hyposalivation sequelae list 'easy exam questions' — distinction from xerostomia (which causes none of these) is direct and tested
items.rendered_text_snippet: Hyposalivation clinical sequelae (all 6): caries, recurrent decay, candidiasis, dysphagia, mucosal trauma, difficulty wearing dentures. Xerostomia alone causes NONE of these.

items.topic: Three questions to ask dry-mouth patient
items.prof_intent: Prof gave class three screening questions mapping to top 3 causes of hyposalivation
items.rendered_text_snippet: Dry-mouth workup questions: (1) Are you anxious? (2) Do you take many medications? (3) Are you dehydrated? = top 3 causes: anxiety, polypharmacy, dehydration.

items.topic: Salivary gland cell waterfall mnemonic
items.prof_intent: Prof introduced waterfall mnemonic to anchor parotid (serous, fast) → submandibular → sublingual (mucous, slow) hierarchy
items.rendered_text_snippet: Waterfall mnemonic: parotid = fast-moving serous water; sublingual = still lagoon mucous. Hierarchy: parotid → submandibular → sublingual.

items.topic: Bilateral vs unilateral Sjögren swelling — bilateral reassuring
items.prof_intent: Prof underscored bilateral = reassuring; unilateral = red flag for MALT transformation
items.rendered_text_snippet: Bilateral salivary gland swelling in Sjögren = generally reassuring. Unilateral = red flag → urgent rheumatology/hematology referral.
